name: Bremerton
tax_rate: 2% special hotel/motel tax (state-credited; WA DOR rate list, verify current)
deadline_pattern: Late August (applications open early August, due about three weeks later at 2 PM); LTAC scores in September, applicant interviews late September, recommendations to Council late October, award notices early November
contact: Bremerton City Council, city.council@bremertonwa.gov, (360) 473-5280; contracts: Jon Hickling, Contracts Administrator
notes: Competitive grants for 2026 totaled $450K across 17 awardees from 20 requests ($1.36M asked); separate budget earmarks of $250K for the Kitsap Conference Center and $150K for the Admiral Theatre; reimbursement-based and applicants must be at least one year old.

presentation.pattern: Applicants selected for interview are notified about two weeks after the deadline and present to LTAC over two days in late September (Sept 21 and 22 for the 2027 cycle)

meeting_schedule: Meets during the fall funding cycle (scoring in September, deliberations in October); next meeting Monday Nov 9, 2026 to finalize recommendations; 6th Floor Council Conference Room, 345 6th St

funding_docs.title: 2027 Lodging Tax Application Instructions
funding_docs.summary: Six funding categories (event marketing, DMO readiness, event development, sports tourism, destination marketing, tourism assets) with Council setting aside 50% of available funds for DMO readiness and sports tourism; 100-point scoring led by tourism priorities (20) and visitor economy impact (20); reimbursement-based, no fixed match, no per-applicant cap, applications due Aug 26, 2026 at 2 PM.

funding_docs.title: Summary of 2026 Lodging Tax Funding Requests and LTAC Funding Recommendations
funding_docs.summary: $1,363,885 requested across 20 applicants and $450,000 recommended and approved by Council Feb 25, 2026; largest awards Downtown Bremerton Association $70K, Sunny Jack Events $65K, Bremerton Historic Ships Association $50K and Greater Kitsap Chamber/Visit Kitsap Peninsula $50K (which had asked for $388,600).

funding_docs.title: LTAC Agenda, Feb 19, 2026 (reconsideration of 2026 funding recommendations)
funding_docs.summary: Special LTAC meeting called after Council rejected the first recommendations on Feb 4, 2026; the committee reaffirmed the same $450K allocation unchanged.

funding_docs.title: 2027 Lodging Tax Award Contract (template)
funding_docs.summary: Standard reimbursement contract awardees sign; no funds may be spent or reimbursed before full execution and contracts over $100,000 need Council approval.

pool_note: 2026: $850K total lodging tax commitments ($450K competitive awards plus $250K Kitsap Conference Center and $150K Admiral Theatre budget earmarks); of the $450K, $25K went to the city's own Quincy Square, leaving $425K awarded to 16 outside applicants.

name: Port Orchard
tax_rate: 2% special hotel/motel tax (state-credited; WA DOR rate list, verify current)
deadline_pattern: Late October at 2 PM (Oct 26, 2026 for 2027 funds); LTAC convenes in the fall to hear applicant presentations and deliberate, then recommends to Council
contact: Megan Hansen, City of Port Orchard, communications@portorchardwa.gov, 360-300-1150; staff liaison City Clerk, 360-876-4407
notes: 2027 application (3-page limit plus financials and marketing samples) is emailed to communications@portorchardwa.gov by Oct 26, 2026 at 2 PM, with LTAC interviews in November; no published pool figure.

presentation.pattern: Eligible applicants may be asked to interview with LTAC in November after the late-October deadline (presentations meeting was Oct 30 in the 2024 cycle), at City Hall with a Zoom webinar option

meeting_schedule: Meets as needed, generally starting in the fall; agendas and minutes on lf.portorchardwa.gov

funding_docs.title: 2027 Lodging Tax Application (acknowledgement, checklist, coversheet and instructions)
funding_docs.summary: Applications due by email Oct 26, 2026 at 2 PM, limited to 3 pages plus attachments (LTAC budget with top 3 priorities, up to 5 marketing samples, 2025 and 2026 YTD financials, tax return); applicants must estimate total visitors, overnight stays, 50+ mile visitors and revenue, and may be interviewed by LTAC in November; no total pool or cap stated.

funding_docs.title: Port Orchard Electronic Records Library: LTAC agendas, minutes and packets
funding_docs.summary: Repository for LTAC agenda packets and minutes including prior-year funding tables; the specific 2026 award list was not retrievable in this pass.

pool_note: No revenue figure, adopted pool or 2026 award list was retrievable; the 2027 application packet states no total.

name: Bainbridge Island
tax_rate: 2% special hotel/motel tax (state-credited; WA DOR rate list, verify current)
deadline_pattern: Historically an RFP issued in late July with proposals due mid-September (4 PM) and presentations late September; the 2026 cycle was delayed, with LTAC hearing all applicants in March 2026 and Council approving awards April 14, 2026
typical_open: Late July or early August (varies; 2026 cycle ran in early spring)
notes: Civic Improvement Fund RFP under BIMC 3.65.040; 2026 awards of $400K went to 11 of 13 applicants ($660K requested), with a $2,000 minimum and a cap of 50% of the pool; the city LTAC page could not be fetched so the current 2027 timeline is unconfirmed.

presentation.pattern: LTAC meets each applicant and hears presentations at scheduled evening meetings at City Hall (280 Madison Ave N) after the deadline; three meetings in March 2026 for the 2026 cycle

meeting_schedule: Meets as needed during the funding cycle (orientation, presentation and deliberation meetings), City Hall, 280 Madison Ave N

funding_docs.title: 2020 Request for Proposals, Civic Improvement Fund (Lodging Tax)
funding_docs.summary: About $275,000 available with a $2,000 minimum and a cap of 50% of funds ($137,500); eligible categories are tourism marketing, special event marketing and operations, tourism facility operations and capital; proposals due mid-September with presentations two weeks later (older cycle; current RFP not retrieved).

funding_docs.title: Bainbridge Island Review: $400K in 2026 lodging tax awards approved April 14, 2026
funding_docs.summary: Council approved $400,000 to 11 of 13 applicants ($659,735 requested) at LTAC-recommended amounts, led by Visit Bainbridge Island $165K, Chamber of Commerce $90K and Downtown Association $70K; Bainbridge Prepares and the Washington Museum Association received nothing.

pool_note: 2026: $400K awarded through the Civic Improvement Fund RFP; $165K to Visit Bainbridge Island and $90K to the Chamber of Commerce are DMO/chamber-type awards, leaving about $145K across nine other outside organizations (estimate, since the DMO and chamber compete in the same round).

name: Sequim
tax_rate: 4% total (2% state-credited plus 2% additional, per 2009 reporting; verify current)
contact: Barbara Hanna, Communications and Marketing Director, City of Sequim, bhanna@sequimwa.gov, 360-681-3422
notes: Sequim has an LTAC (SMC 2.68, chaired by a councilmember, meets quarterly) but no standing open grant round was found; the city ran one-off $50K Tourism Sustainability Grant rounds ($5K max) in 2020, 2021 and 2022 and otherwise directs lodging tax to city marketing and the visitor center.
meeting_schedule: Quarterly (per city announcements); minutes go to Council at least quarterly

alternatives.administrator: Clallam County Board of Commissioners / Clallam County LTAC
alternatives.funds: About $2M a year in lodging tax grants countywide; $204K awarded to 7 organizations in the spring 2025 round
alternatives.eligibility: Nonprofits, public entities and groups of eligible organizations with projects that put heads in beds; must report overnight stays
alternatives.deadline_pattern: Fall call due around Oct 11 (noon) for the next year, plus a second call in January or February (2026 notice listed Feb 13 and Feb 26); a 2027 call for applications is posted
alternatives.contact: Loni Gores, Clerk of the Board, loni.gores@clallamcountywa.gov, 360-417-2256
alternatives.notes: LTAC meets the second Thursday monthly at 2 PM in Room 160, 223 E 4th St, Port Angeles; prosecuting attorney screens applications for eligibility; Sequim-based events such as the Irrigation Festival have been funded.

alternatives.program: Olympic Peninsula Visitor Bureau Tourism Project Grants
alternatives.eligibility: Shoulder-season tourism projects, collateral, event promotion and websites primarily within Clallam County
alternatives.deadline_pattern: Historically reviewed up to four times a year, due two weeks before a board meeting
alternatives.notes: Details are from 2018 reporting; confirm the program is still active.

funding_docs.title: Sequim Municipal Code Chapter 2.68, Lodging Tax Advisory Committee
funding_docs.summary: Establishes the five-plus member LTAC chaired by a councilmember with equal lodging and activity representation; LTAC reviews any change in lodging tax use within 45 days and reports on long-term stability of the lodging tax fund, but the code sets no grant program.

funding_docs.title: Sequim Gazette: Council approves $50,000 Tourism Sustainability Grant round (March 30, 2022)
funding_docs.summary: One-off round of up to $5,000 per nonprofit tourism organization within the Sequim School District, $50K total from city lodging tax, applications due April 15, 2022 with LTAC review April 20 and Council action April 25.

pool_note: No standing competitive round; the city's 4% lodging tax funds its own marketing and visitor center contract, and the only outside grants were one-off $50K Tourism Sustainability rounds in 2020-2022 (annual revenue not published).

name: Port Townsend
tax_rate: 2% special hotel/motel tax (state-credited; WA DOR rate list, verify current)
deadline_pattern: One round for 2026: call issued Dec 1 with applications due the first Monday of January at 5 PM and review at the January LTAC meeting; in 2024 there were spring (late Feb) and fall (late Aug) rounds
notes: Awards run $1,000 to $10,000 per project with priority on shoulder-season (Oct through May) overnight visitors and lodging partnerships; prior-year recipients must wait a year before reapplying; the 2027 call had not been posted as of this research.

presentation.pattern: Applicants attend the grant review meeting (second Tuesday after the deadline, 3 PM) to give a 3-minute overview and answer questions

meeting_schedule: Second Tuesday of odd-numbered months at 3 PM, City Council Chambers, Historic City Hall, 540 Water St

funding_docs.title: Press release: LTAC announces $50,000 in grant funding for 2026 (Dec 1, 2025)
funding_docs.summary: $50,000 available in a single 2026 round with awards of $1,000 to $10,000; applications due Jan 5, 2026 at 5 PM and reviewed at the Jan 13 LTAC meeting; priority on shoulder-season (Oct through May) overnight visitors, local jobs and lodging partnerships.

funding_docs.title: LTAC Grant Program webinar slides (January 2024)
funding_docs.summary: 2024 grants were $40,000 within a $530,000 LTAC budget (2023: $20,000 granted against $60,700 requested, awards $800 to $7,000); scored on overnight stays, off-season timing, new offerings under 3 years old, local jobs, partnerships and leveraged match, with applicants giving a 3-minute overview at the review meeting.

funding_docs.title: Lodging Tax Advisory Committee program page
funding_docs.summary: Lists the $40K two-round program, $1K to $10K award range, one-year wait for prior recipients, portal rules and that 2022 city lodging tax collections were $602,167 supporting marketing, events, infrastructure, fee waivers and debt service.

pool_note: 2026: $50K grant round for outside organizations; the 2024 LTAC budget was $530K with the balance committed to city marketing, events, infrastructure, fee waivers and debt service (total is the 2024 figure).

name: Forks
tax_rate: 2% special hotel/motel tax (state-credited; WA DOR rate list, verify current)
deadline_pattern: Late September at 5 PM (Sept 26, 2022 for 2023; Sept 23, 2024 for 2025), with City Council review of all proposals at a public meeting in mid to late November as part of the budget
contact: Caryn DePew, Clerk/Treasurer, City of Forks, 500 E Division St, Forks, WA 98331
notes: Forks (under 5,000 population) has no separate LTAC; applications go to the Clerk/Treasurer and the City Council reviews them in budget workshops, with 24 requests totaling about $500K in the 2024 cycle; reimbursement only, no multi-year commitments; the 2026 and 2027 application packets were not located.

presentation.pattern: City Council reviews proposals at a public meeting in November (Nov 25, 2024 at 5:30 PM for the 2025 cycle); applicants may attend but no formal presentation is required

meeting_schedule: No LTAC; City Council budget workshops in November and December

funding_docs.title: City of Forks Lodging Tax Application 2025
funding_docs.summary: Applications due Sept 23, 2024 at 5 PM to the Clerk/Treasurer; Lodging Tax Fund is the city's sole tourism funding source, reimbursement only after the event with payment requested within 60 days, no multi-year commitments and the city sets the spendable amount each year; Council review Nov 25, 2024.

funding_docs.title: City of Forks Lodging Tax Application 2023
funding_docs.summary: Prior-year packet with the same structure: due Sept 26, 2022, Council review Nov 14, 2022, post-event economic impact report due Jan 29, 2024.

funding_docs.title: Peninsula Daily News: Forks reviews 2024 draft budget and lodging tax requests (Dec 2, 2023)
funding_docs.summary: 24 requests totaling about $500,000 against $503,233 collected through October 2023; largest asks were Forks Chamber of Commerce $185,000 (Twilight Festival, visitor center and marketing) and City of Forks $169,175 (Fourth of July, ball fields, Rainforest Arts Center), with Forks Timber Museum $35,000.

pool_note: 2024 cycle: about $503K collected through October 2023 against roughly $500K in 24 requests, dominated by the Forks Chamber ($185K visitor center, marketing and Twilight events) and the city's own $169K; final awards to the remaining smaller applicants (about $62.5K requested) were not published, so no competitive figure.

name: Anacortes
deadline_pattern: Applications solicited each year in the fall with Council adopting awards by resolution in early December (Resolution 3191 on Dec 8, 2025 for 2026)
contact: Stephanie Snyder, Program Coordinator, City of Anacortes, 360-293-1907
notes: 2026 awards totaled $693,800 ($327,300 for annual events and marketing plus $366,500 capital for the city event center design); most grants are $5,000 to $25,000 and Council may only pick from LTAC's list; the 2027 application deadline was not published on the page.
meeting_schedule: No regular schedule; meetings publicly noticed as needed (orientation in February, review in the fall)

funding_docs.title: Resolution 3191, Approved 2026 Funding for Tourism Promotion
funding_docs.summary: Adopted Dec 8, 2025: $693,800 total, $327,300 for annual projects and $366,500 capital for the city Event Center design; largest annual awards Experience Anacortes marketing $130,000, Chamber events $44,000, Visitor Information Center $25,000 and park restroom maintenance $25,000; three requests got $0.

funding_docs.title: LTAC Orientation, Feb 22, 2024
funding_docs.summary: 4% lodging tax yields about $650K a year with about $1.5M in reserve; the 2023 Tourism Promotion Strategic Plan targets holding 25% in reserve for capital projects; LTAC recommendations must address tourism benefit, fund stability, request-to-attendance ratio, statutory eligibility and the applicant's reporting history.

funding_docs.title: Lodging Tax Advisory Committee page (program overview)
funding_docs.summary: States the 4% tax, annual solicitation, RCW 67.28.1816 eligible uses and that most grants are $5,000 to $25,000; links the 2023-2028 Tourism Promotion Plan (Resolution 3138).

pool_note: 2026: $693,800 awarded by Resolution 3191; after $366,500 city Event Center capital, $40K city parks items and $202K to the Chamber (Experience Anacortes marketing, visitor center, chamber events and Walk Fest), about $85K went to 15 other outside applicants.

name: Oak Harbor
tax_rate: 2% special hotel/motel tax (state-credited; WA DOR rate list, verify current)
deadline_pattern: Mid-August at 4:30 PM (Aug 14, 2026 for 2027 funds); LTAC deliberates in November and Council adopts awards by resolution
contact: David Goldman, Deputy City Administrator/Finance Director (LTAC liaison), City of Oak Harbor, 360-279-4500; Wendy Horn, Grants Administrator
notes: Tourism Promotion Grant open to any entity type for public events and promotion inside city limits; Council approved $475K for 2026 with 21 applications near $800K and 15 funded, including a multi-year city award.

members.name: Tara Hizon
members.affiliation: Mayor Pro Tem, Oak Harbor City Council

members.name: David Goldman
members.affiliation: City of Oak Harbor, Deputy City Administrator/Finance Director

presentation.pattern: LTAC may ask applicants to present at a scheduled meeting; staff email applicants to schedule times

meeting_schedule: As needed, posted at least 10 days ahead; next meeting Thursday Nov 12, 2026 at 10 AM to deliberate 2027 funding, 865 SE Barrington Dr

funding_docs.title: Lodging Tax / Tourism Promotion Grant program page
funding_docs.summary: 2027 applications were due Aug 14, 2026 at 4:30 PM; any entity type may apply for public events and promotion inside city limits under RCW 67.28.1816 uses; LTAC deliberates Nov 12, 2026 and Council must adopt the recommendations by resolution.

funding_docs.title: Council approves most LTAC lodging tax awards, sends marina debt service item back (Nov 19, 2025)
funding_docs.summary: Council had approved $475,000 for 2026 with $50,000 earmarked for Whidbey and Camano Islands tourism; 21 applications near $800,000 with 15 recommended for about $408,000, and a $55,000 marina debt-service request returned to LTAC for a 45-day review.

funding_docs.title: LTAC minutes, Feb 4, 2025 (2026 application scoring revisions)
funding_docs.summary: Committee revised the 2026 application questions and point values and reordered them; staff drafted the changes for the August 2025 kickoff of the 2026 cycle.

pool_note: 2026: Council approved $475K; staff and LTAC recommended about $408K to 15 of 21 applicants, which included a $55K city marina debt-service item, leaving roughly $353K for outside applicants (estimate; a $50K Whidbey and Camano tourism earmark may also sit inside that figure).

name: Friday Harbor
tax_rate: 2% special hotel/motel tax (state-credited; WA DOR rate list, verify current)
deadline_pattern: LTAC planning meeting in May, RFP and application released in June for the following year; exact due date not published on the page (contact LTAC Coordinator); urgent off-cycle requests go to Town Council via a separate form
contact: Julie Greene, LTAC Coordinator, Town of Friday Harbor, julie@fridayharbor.org, (360) 378-2810 ext. 1229
notes: Grants promote Friday Harbor events and activities that attract visitors; 2027 applications were released in June 2026 and the window is now closed, with reimbursement requests from 2026 recipients due Jan 5, 2027 and attendance reports Jan 31, 2027.

members.name: Julie Greene
members.affiliation: Town of Friday Harbor, LTAC Coordinator

meeting_schedule: As needed; planning meeting each May; agendas posted before meetings

funding_docs.title: Lodging Tax Grant Application page (example RFP, forms and reporting notices)
funding_docs.summary: Grants promote Friday Harbor events and activities that attract visitors, funded by the hotel/motel tax on all transient lodging; 2027 applications released June 2026 after a May planning meeting; reimbursement requests from 2026 awardees due Jan 5, 2027 and attendance reports Jan 31, 2027; an urgent off-cycle request form goes to Town Council; no pool total published.

pool_note: The town publishes no pool total or award list on its LTAC page; contact the LTAC Coordinator for current figures.

name: Westport
tax_rate: 5% special excise tax on lodging (WMC 3.42.020; first 2% state-credited)
notes: Westport (population under 5,000) levies a 5% lodging tax into a city tourism fund under WMC 3.42 but no published LTAC, grant application or deadline was found; funding requests appear to go directly to the City Council through the budget process.

alternatives.program: City of Westport tourism fund request via City Council
alternatives.administrator: City of Westport (City Clerk / City Council)
alternatives.eligibility: Activities that attract visitors, special events and festivals, and tourism-related facilities per WMC 3.42.050 and RCW 67.28
alternatives.deadline_pattern: Requests considered during fall budget preparation
alternatives.notes: No application form or schedule located; contact Westport City Hall to request inclusion in the lodging tax budget.

alternatives.program: Grays Harbor County Lodging Tax grants
alternatives.administrator: Grays Harbor County Commissioners / County LTAC
alternatives.eligibility: Tourism promotion and events in Grays Harbor County
alternatives.notes: Not verified in this research pass; confirm with the Grays Harbor County Commissioners' office.

funding_docs.title: Westport Municipal Code Chapter 3.42, Special Excise Tax on Lodging
funding_docs.summary: Levies a 5% lodging excise tax (first 2% credited against state sales tax) into a dedicated city fund for attracting visitors, marketing and operating special events and festivals, and tourism facility operations and capital per RCW 67.28.1815; no grant process is defined.

pool_note: 5% city lodging tax revenue and its commitments are not published online; no grant program or award list was found.
